clue.text: In Caracas sat awaiting ice cream

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone in the Venezuelan capital sits waiting for a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of Caracas through sat into the start of awaiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian dessert of layered frozen cream with candied fruit, a kind of iced confection.

clue.text: Talk about energy fraud

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to talk casually is to chat
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A conversation about an energy scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is a swindler, someone who deceives for gain, a fraud.

clue.text: Back Companion of Honour over warning colour in House of Lords perhaps

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the preceding pieces sit above the next

parts.note: to back a motion is to second it
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order
amber is the warning light on traffic signals

explanation.surface: Supporting a decorated peer over a warning colour in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lords is an example of an upper house of a two-house parliament, the revising chamber, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Dad upset over friend's dismay

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the next
upset in a down clue means the word for dad is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: dad is pa
a friend is a pal; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An upset father worries about a mate's distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock and horrify, filling someone with dismay.

clue.text: Are gripping rascal in shopping precinct

indicators.note: gripping means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rascal

explanation.surface: Are you holding on to a scoundrel in the shopping centre?
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered walk lined with shops, a shopping precinct.

clue.text: Exchange involving Mike's waterlogged area

indicators.note: involving means the first word wraps round the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to exchange is to swap
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A trade in which Mike gets a soggy plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp is boggy ground permanently soaked with water, a marsh.

clue.text: Soapy liquid not what it seems, poor, ultimately lacking

parts.note: a sham is a fake, something not what it seems

indicators.note: ultimately lacking means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A hair wash that is fake and cheap, missing its final ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap preparation for washing hair.

clue.text: The cartoonist upset, having little advance warning

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the words before it are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cartoonist is put out by being given hardly any warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged hastily, with almost no prior notice, happens at short notice.

clue.text: Pioneering chemist super at broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A trailblazing scientist is praised as super on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist who pioneered pasteurisation and germ theory.

clue.text: Defective seascapes clue? These might give way out

indicators.note: something defective is faulty, so the letters that follow are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A faulty crossword clue about sea paintings, wondering if it offers an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract provisions that let a party withdraw under set conditions offer a legal exit, a way out of the deal.

clue.text: Complicated time: old invader departs

parts.note: the Angles were Germanic invaders of early Britain
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A tricky moment: an ancient invader leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something knotted and intertwined is complicated, hard to sort out.

clue.text: Speaker's arguments for ordinary writing

indicators.note: a speaker's version is how the words are said aloud, so the answer sounds like them

parts.note: arguments in favour are pros, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A speaker's case in favour of plain written language.
explanation.definitionFit: Prose is written language in its everyday form, without the metre of verse.

clue.text: Succeeded at first with aloof manner in island

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: behaving coldly and distantly is acting icily

explanation.surface: Someone who did well early on, while keeping a cool reserve on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Mediterranean island off the toe of Italy.

clue.text: Refuse to leave street? Indeed, sulk forgetting nothing

parts.note: ay is an old word for yes, indeed

indicators.note: forgetting means the word for nothing is left out of the word for sulk

parts.note: to sulk is to pout
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A resident won't move out of the road; yes, they sulk about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain where one is, declining to go anywhere, is to stay in place.

clue.text: Large upper room with Eastern ornamental pattern

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an attic is a room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: A big loft room decorated with an oriental design.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework of strips forming a decorative pattern.

clue.text: Somewhat retro, stereotyped, work list

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rota that seems old-fashioned and clichéd.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster is a schedule assigning duties to people, a rota of who works when.

clue.text: Roughly hustle investigator

indicators.note: roughly means handled crudely, so the letters of the next word are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective shoves someone roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, one who investigates crimes.

clue.text: Make changes in plug fitting

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad
fitting means suitable, apt

explanation.surface: Alter something inside an electrical plug that fits a socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug fitting' reads as electrical hardware, but plug is an advert and fitting means suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify something to suit new conditions, altering it.

clue.text: Agile learner lives a bit

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on British learner drivers' cars
lives means exists, is
a bit of something is some of it

explanation.surface: A nimble student lives a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes a body that is supple and lithe, moving easily and nimbly.

clue.text: Pole's second attempt to win

parts.note: to have a tilt at something is to make an attempt at winning it

explanation.surface: A Polish competitor's second go at victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a long stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A stilt is a long upright post, one of the poles a walker stands on to gain height.

clue.text: Country for example you passed through initially

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A country, for instance, that you travelled through at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is the North African nation on the Nile, a country.

clue.text: Well-known type of room for water board?

parts.note: something well known is public knowledge
a utility room houses the washing machine and similar appliances

explanation.surface: A famous kind of room serving as a water board, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A water supply company is an example of an organisation providing an essential service to all, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Left-winger returning with English cake

indicators.note: returning means the word for the left-winger is read backwards

parts.note: a Trot is short for a Trotskyist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: A socialist comes back with an English cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered gateau of Central European style, a type of cake.

clue.text: Difficult situation of throaty Sue, pasty regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words before it, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Hoarse-voiced, pale Sue finds herself in a tricky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat means being under pressure in an uncomfortable position, a difficult situation.
